description:
FOUND s500 (Fable, 2026-09-28) by ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s500/review/r500p-float.pl (out/r500p-float.{perl,base}, rows 2 and 33).  PRE-EXISTING on main 209e7533.  Both rare; filed so the perf agent (s500p, float->text) does not silently change either direction without a task.

(1) NEGATIVE ZERO:  printf "%g|%e|%f|%.0f|%+.1e|%08.3f|%s\n", (-0.0) x 7;
    perl: -0|-0.000000e+00|-0.000000|-0|-0.0e+00|-000.000|0        (perl's own stringification `%s`/`print` gives "0"; only the C-printf conversions keep the sign)
    PCL :  0| 0.000000e+00| 0.000000| 0|+0.0e+00|0000.000|0
  Perl-shaped: the sprintf conversions receive the double and C prints its sign; `print` goes through %.15g's Gconvert which drops it.  Fix in the sprintf float conversions only (`p-sprintf`'s %g/%e/%f arms): test `(minusp (float-sign x))`, never the value.  Note `-0.0 ** 3` and `(-0.0) ** 3` print `0` in both (r500p-pow.pl) -- unchanged.

(2) DENORMAL LITERAL:  print 4.9e-324, " ", 5e-324, " ", 2.2250738585072014e-308, "\n";
    perl: 4.94065645841247e-324 4.94065645841247e-324 2.2250738585072e-308
    PCL : 0 4.94065645841247e-324 2.2250738585072e-308
  The literal 4.9e-324 (below the smallest denormal's shortest spelling, but a legal C strtod input that rounds UP to 5e-324) becomes 0 -- either the emitted CL literal (`4.9d-324`) is read by SBCL as 0 (SBCL's reader underflow for a non-representable denormal -- probe `(read-from-string "4.9d-324")` with `sb-ext:*read-default-float-format*`) or the compiler's own number normaliser zeroes it.  Fix at whichever layer turns the TEXT into a double: perl's rule is strtod (round to nearest representable, denormals included).  Probe `1e-320`, `2e-324`, `2.5e-324` (perl: 0? -- probe), `1e-400` (0), `-4.9e-324`.
  Not #1513 (that is the boundless INTEGER model); not #1515.
